commitments.quote: "Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304, limited to incidents involving ePHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors create, receive, maintain or transmit for Covered Entity.
commitments.summary: Security Incident reporting covers only incidents involving ePHI that the vendor or its Subcontractors handle for the Covered Entity.
commitments.scope: Only incidents involving ePHI created, received, maintained or transmitted for Covered Entity by Business Associate or its Subcontractors. The definition in 45 C.F.R. § 164.304 is incorporated by reference and is not reproduced in the contract.
commitments.deviation: The DPA defines Personal Data Breach as a confirmed breach affecting Customer Personal Data and excludes unsuccessful attempts. The BAA defines Security Incident by reference to the HIPAA regulation and limits it to ePHI, and it does not require the incident to be confirmed.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as permitted by this BAA.
commitments.summary: The vendor may use and disclose PHI only to perform the Underlying Agreements, as required by law, or as this BAA permits.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including limited data sets (Section 2.4).
commitments.deviation: The DPA limits processing to Customer's documented instructions. The BAA limits use and disclosure to performance of the Underlying Agreements, legal requirements, or BAA permissions.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.summary: The vendor must limit its uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
commitments.scope: All PHI.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate may de-identify PHI only in accordance with the safe harbor method at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)(2), and may use the de-identified information only to provide and improve the services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.summary: The vendor may de-identify PHI only by the HIPAA safe harbor method and may use the result only to provide and improve services under the Underlying Agreements.
commitments.scope: De-identified information derived from PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA lets ExampleCo use aggregated or de-identified Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services. The BAA requires the safe harbor method and limits use of de-identified data to providing and improving services under the Underlying Agreements, which excludes the DPA's security use. The BAA has no express restriction on training models.

commitments.quote: Information de-identified in accordance with this Section 2.3 is not PHI and is not subject to this BAA.
commitments.summary: Information de-identified under Section 2.3 is not PHI and falls outside the BAA.
commitments.scope: Only information de-identified per the safe harbor method in Section 2.3. Other de-identified data remains PHI (this is an inference from the wording).
commitments.deviation: The DPA's Usage Data definition excludes aggregated or de-identified data that does not identify Customer or any person. The BAA's carve-out is narrower because it applies only to safe harbor de-identification.

commitments.quote: A limited data set under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e) is PHI for all purposes of this BAA.
commitments.summary: A limited data set counts as PHI for all BAA purposes, so all BAA duties apply to it.
commitments.scope: Limited data sets as defined at 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e).
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Personal Data in Customer Data and has no limited data set concept. Here the data covered is expanded to include limited data sets.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 C.F.R. Part 164 with respect to ePHI.
commitments.summary: The vendor must comply with the HIPAA Security Rule (Subpart C) for ePHI.
commitments.scope: ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the measures in Annex 2, which the vendor may update. The BAA requires compliance with the HIPAA Security Rule and lists no specific controls such as AES-256, TLS or MFA.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: The vendor must not store PHI outside the United States.
commitments.scope: All PHI, with storage and processing restricted to the US.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data in the region Customer selects. The BAA fixes storage and processing in the United States.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall not store, process or access PHI outside the United States.
commitments.summary: The vendor must not access PHI from outside the United States, which rules out offshore support access such as from Manila.
commitments.scope: All PHI, including access by personnel and Subcontractors. The Subcontractor reach follows from Section 5.1 flow-down and is an inference.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits access from outside the hosting region, including from Manila, Philippines. The BAA prohibits all access to PHI from outside the United States and has no exception for support, maintenance or security operations.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall maintain HITRUST r2 certification for the systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.summary: The vendor must maintain HITRUST r2 certification for systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.scope: Systems that store or process PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification. The BAA requires HITRUST r2 certification and does not mention SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and in no event later than ten (10) calendar days after Discovery.
commitments.summary: The vendor must report any Breach of Unsecured PHI without unreasonable delay and no later than 10 calendar days after Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery of the Breach, as defined in the HIPAA Rules incorporated by Section 1.1. Under 45 C.F.R. § 164.410, which the BAA does not reproduce, this is when the Breach is known or reasonably should have been known to the vendor.

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Breaches of Unsecured PHI. This is narrower than all PHI incidents.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires notice within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach. The BAA allows 10 calendar days after Discovery, and Discovery can arise from what the vendor should reasonably have known rather than only from confirmation. This is a longer outer limit.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any Security Incident within five (5) business days after Business Associate becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: The vendor must report any Security Incident within 5 business days after it becomes aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becoming aware of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving ePHI handled for Covered Entity by Business Associate or its Subcontractors (Section 1.2).
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no separate Security Incident report and its 72-hour clock runs only from confirmed Personal Data Breaches. The BAA adds a 5-business-day report for Security Incidents running from awareness.

commitments.quote: This Section 4.2 serves as notice of, and no further report is required for, unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-in attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.summary: The BAA itself is standing notice of unsuccessful attempts such as pings, port scans and blocked log-ins, so no further report is needed for them.
commitments.scope: Unsuccessful attempts that do not result in unauthorized access to ePHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA excludes unsuccessful attempts from Personal Data Breach altogether. The BAA treats them as Security Incidents but deems them already notified.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this BAA within ten (10) calendar days after becoming aware of it.
commitments.summary: The vendor must report any use or disclosure of PHI not permitted by the BAA within 10 calendar days after becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Business Associate becoming aware of the unauthorized use or disclosure

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by the BAA, whether or not it is a Breach.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA requires notice only of confirmed Personal Data Breaches.

commitments.quote: Reports under this Section 4 shall be made in writing to Covered Entity's Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to its Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example.
commitments.summary: All Section 4 reports must be made in writing to the Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office.
commitments.recipient: Privacy Office at privacy-office@ahs.example, with a copy to the Information Security Office at iso@ahs.example
commitments.scope: Breach, Security Incident and unauthorized use or disclosure reports under Section 4.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the security contact designated in the administration console, or else the account owner. The BAA names two fixed email addresses and requires written notice.

commitments.quote: A report of a Breach shall include, to the extent known, the identity of each individual affected, the PHI involved, the date of the Breach and of its Discovery, and the steps taken to mitigate it.
commitments.summary: A Breach report must include, to the extent known, the affected individuals, the PHI involved, the Breach and Discovery dates, and mitigation steps.
commitments.recipient: Covered Entity's Privacy Office, with a copy to the Information Security Office (Section 4.4)
commitments.scope: Breach reports only, not Security Incident or unauthorized use reports.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires the nature of the breach, the data categories affected and the measures taken, plus further information as it becomes available. The BAA requires more specific content, including the identity of each affected individual and the dates, but has no express duty to supplement the report.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: The vendor must reimburse Covered Entity's reasonable costs of notifying individuals, regulators and the media of a Breach it or its Subcontractors caused.
commitments.scope: Breaches caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors, limited to notification costs.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent. The DPA is silent on incident costs and says its breach notice is not an admission of fault.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on its behalf agrees in writing to the same restrictions and conditions that apply to Business Associate under this BAA.
commitments.summary: The vendor must make each Subcontractor handling PHI agree in writing to the same restrictions and conditions as the BAA.
commitments.scope: Subcontractors as defined in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103 that handle PHI for the vendor.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives general authorization, 30 days' notice of new Subprocessors, a 15-day objection right and vendor responsibility for them. The BAA has none of the notice or objection terms and instead requires written flow-down of the BAA's restrictions.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within ten (10) business days after Covered Entity's request, so Covered Entity can meet 45 C.F.R. § 164.524.
commitments.summary: The vendor must make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Covered Entity within 10 business days after its request. The closest listed type is security_controls, but this is an individual-rights access duty.

deadline.anchor: Covered Entity's request

commitments.scope: PHI in a Designated Record Set.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of determining compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
commitments.summary: The vendor must make its internal practices, books and records relating to PHI available to the HHS Secretary to determine HIPAA compliance.
commitments.recipient: Secretary of Health and Human Services
commitments.scope: Internal practices, books and records relating to PHI.
commitments.deviation: The DPA provides audit reports and a regulator-driven on-site audit for the Customer. The BAA gives government access to books and records and has no Customer audit right, SOC 2 report or penetration test summary commitment.

commitments.quote: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, Business Associate shall return or destroy all PHI within thirty (30) days.
commitments.summary: On termination of the Underlying Agreements, the vendor must return or destroy all PHI within 30 days.

deadline.anchor: Termination of the Underlying Agreements

commitments.recipient: Covered Entity (inference: return goes to Covered Entity)
commitments.scope: All PHI. The BAA does not mention backups.
commitments.deviation: The DPA deletes within 90 days after termination of the Agreement, with backups overwritten within a further 35 days. The BAA allows 30 days, offers return or destruction, has no backup allowance, and has no deletion certification term as the DPA's 10.2 does.

commitments.quote: If return or destruction is not feasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this BAA to that PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.summary: If return or destruction is not feasible, the vendor must keep applying the BAA's protections to the PHI for as long as it retains it.
commitments.scope: PHI that cannot feasibly be returned or destroyed.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no infeasibility exception, though it allows backups to persist for 35 days. The BAA lets the vendor retain PHI indefinitely if return or destruction is infeasible, with the BAA protections continuing.

commitments.quote: This VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and over any data processing terms, policies or online terms of Vendor or its Affiliates.
commitments.summary: The VDPA takes precedence over the Subscription Agreement and any Vendor or Affiliate data processing, policy or online terms.
commitments.scope: Applies to the Subscription Agreement and all Vendor and Affiliate data processing terms, policies and online terms, including ExampleCo's standard DPA (inference: ExampleCo is a Vendor Affiliate per Appendix B Amendment No. 1).
commitments.deviation: Baseline DPA controls over the Agreement only as to Customer Personal Data; here the VDPA prevails over the Subscription Agreement and also over the Vendor's and Affiliates' own DPA, policy and online terms, and is not limited to personal data.

commitments.quote: "Retailer Data" means all data that Retailer, its employees or its customers provide to Vendor or that Vendor collects from Retailer's systems, including telemetry, logs, traces and metrics, and all data derived from any of it.
commitments.summary: Protected data covers all data provided by or collected from Retailer, including telemetry, logs, traces, metrics and derived data, not just personal data.
commitments.scope: All Retailer, employee and customer-provided data, data collected from Retailer systems (telemetry, logs, traces, metrics) and all derived data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline covers only Personal Data within Customer Data; this covers all data including telemetry and derived data, whether or not personal, so it is much broader. Usage Data carve-out in baseline 1.6 has no equivalent.

commitments.quote: "Data Incident" means any actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access to, or acquisition, disclosure or loss of, Retailer Data, including while held by a Subprocessor.
commitments.summary: Defines the incidents that trigger notice to include suspected as well as actual unauthorized access, acquisition, disclosure or loss of Retailer Data, including at Subprocessors.
commitments.scope: Actual or reasonably suspected incidents involving any Retailer Data, including data held by Subprocessors (which include Vendor Affiliates).
commitments.deviation: Baseline Personal Data Breach requires vendor confirmation, is limited to Customer Personal Data, and excludes unsuccessful attempts; this includes reasonably suspected incidents and all Retailer Data, with no express exclusion for unsuccessful attempts.

commitments.quote: "Subprocessor" means any third party, including any Vendor Affiliate, that processes Retailer Data on Vendor's behalf.
commitments.summary: Subprocessors expressly include Vendor Affiliates that process Retailer Data, so Affiliates are subject to the Subprocessor duties.
commitments.scope: Any third party or Vendor Affiliate processing Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline covers third parties processing Customer Personal Data; this expressly includes Vendor Affiliates and covers all Retailer Data.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall process Retailer Data only to provide the services described in the Subscription Agreement (the "Services") and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.summary: Vendor may process Retailer Data only to provide the Services and on Retailer's written instructions.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline allows processing on documented instructions including Customer's configuration of the Services; this requires written instructions and limits processing to providing the Services.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model, except models used only to provide the Services to Retailer.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not use Retailer Data to train or improve any machine learning model other than models used solely to serve Retailer.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data including derived data, telemetry, logs, traces and metrics; any ML model, not only foundation models.
commitments.deviation: Baseline bars only training or fine-tuning foundation models made available to other customers and permits use of aggregated Usage Data to improve the Services; this bars training or improving any ML model except Retailer-only models, with no Usage Data exception.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall store Retailer Data only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.summary: Retailer Data may be stored only in the United States or Canada.
commitments.scope: Storage of all Retailer Data. The contract does not say whether access from other locations is allowed (offshore access not addressed).
commitments.deviation: Baseline stores data in the customer-selected hosting region; this fixes storage to the US or Canada. Baseline 6.2 allows access from outside the region including Manila; this contract has no express access term, only the storage restriction.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards that meet or exceed the CIS Critical Security Controls, Implementation Group 2.
commitments.summary: Vendor must maintain safeguards meeting or exceeding CIS Controls Implementation Group 2.
commitments.deviation: Baseline commits to Annex 2 measures that the vendor may update; this fixes a named external benchmark (CIS IG2) with no unilateral update right.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.summary: Vendor must encrypt Retailer Data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption.
commitments.scope: All Retailer Data.
commitments.deviation: Baseline specifies AES-256 and TLS 1.2 or higher; this requires only unspecified industry-standard encryption.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall obtain a SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services each year and provide it to Retailer within fifteen (15) days after Retailer's request.
commitments.summary: Vendor must obtain a SOC 2 Type II report each year and deliver it to Retailer within 15 days of request.

deadline.anchor: Retailer's request for the SOC 2 Type II report

secondary_deadline.anchor: annual SOC 2 Type II report cycle

commitments.scope: SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.deviation: Baseline maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 and makes the report available via the Trust Center under NDA (9.1); this requires an annual SOC 2 report delivered within 15 days of request and has no ISO 27001 requirement.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not permit any Subprocessor other than those listed in Appendix B to process Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written consent.
commitments.summary: Only Subprocessors listed in Appendix B may process Retailer Data unless Retailer gives prior written consent.
commitments.scope: Appendix B as amended lists AWS, Helpdesk Platform, Inc. and, since Amendment No. 1 (September 8, 2025), ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) for platform hosting and AI features.
commitments.deviation: Baseline gives general authorization to engage Subprocessors; this requires an approved list and prior written consent for others.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall request consent for a new Subprocessor in writing at least thirty (30) days before the Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data. Retailer's silence is not consent.
commitments.summary: Vendor must request written consent at least 30 days before a new Subprocessor starts processing, and silence does not count as consent.

deadline.anchor: new Subprocessor begins processing Retailer Data

commitments.scope: New Subprocessors, including Vendor Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: Baseline gives 30 days' notice via the Trust Center with an objection right and deemed acceptance; this requires a written consent request and silence is not consent. Baseline 5.3 objection and 5.4 urgent-replacement rights have no equivalent, so no urgent replacement without consent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall bind each Subprocessor in writing to obligations at least as protective as this VDPA, and remains liable for each Subprocessor's acts and omissions.
commitments.summary: Vendor must bind each Subprocessor in writing to terms at least as protective as the VDPA and remains liable for their acts and omissions.
commitments.scope: Each Subprocessor, including Vendor Affiliates.
commitments.deviation: Baseline makes ExampleCo responsible for Subprocessor performance of the DPA; this adds a written flow-down requirement and liability for all acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and no later than twenty-four (24) hours after Vendor becomes aware of it.
commitments.summary: Vendor must notify Retailer of a Data Incident without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware of it.

deadline.anchor: Vendor becomes aware of the Data Incident (actual or reasonably suspected)

commitments.scope: Data Incidents, i.e. actual or reasonably suspected unauthorized access, acquisition, disclosure or loss of Retailer Data, including at Subprocessors.
commitments.deviation: Baseline gives 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a breach; this gives 24 hours from awareness, covering suspected incidents. The VDPA prevails over vendor terms (1.1), so 24 hours governs.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall send notice by email to Retailer Security Operations at secops@arg.example and by telephone to +1 (614) 555-0182. Notice to Retailer's account or procurement contacts does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must go by both email and telephone to Retailer Security Operations; notice to account or procurement contacts is insufficient.
commitments.recipient: Retailer Security Operations, secops@arg.example and telephone +1 (614) 555-0182
commitments.scope: Notices of Data Incidents under 6.1.
commitments.deviation: Baseline sends notice to the security contact designated in the console or else the account owner; this fixes a specific email and phone and rejects account or procurement contacts.

commitments.quote: Vendor's notice shall describe the Data Incident, the Retailer Data involved, any Subprocessor involved, and the steps Vendor has taken. Vendor shall supplement the notice as new information becomes available.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must describe the incident, data, any Subprocessor involved and steps taken, and be supplemented as information emerges.
commitments.scope: Data Incident notices.
commitments.deviation: Baseline describes nature, data categories and measures 'to the extent then known'; this also requires identifying any Subprocessor involved and has no 'to the extent known' qualifier. Baseline 7.4 (no admission of fault) has no equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall not inform Retailer's customers or any third party of a Data Incident involving Retailer Data without Retailer's prior written approval, except as required by law.
commitments.summary: Vendor may not tell Retailer's customers or third parties about a Data Incident without Retailer's prior written approval, unless legally required.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents involving Retailer Data; communications to Retailer's customers and any third party.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Vendor shall cooperate with Retailer's investigation and shall bear the reasonable costs of a Data Incident to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.summary: Vendor must cooperate with Retailer's investigation and bear reasonable Data Incident costs to the extent caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors.
commitments.scope: Data Incidents caused by Vendor or its Subprocessors (including Vendor Affiliates).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after the Subscription Agreement ends, Vendor shall delete all Retailer Data and confirm the deletion to Retailer in writing.
commitments.summary: Vendor must delete all Retailer Data within 30 days after the Subscription Agreement ends and confirm deletion in writing.

deadline.anchor: the Subscription Agreement ends

commitments.scope: All Retailer Data, including derived data. No separate backup overwrite period is stated.
commitments.deviation: Baseline allows 90 days plus 35 for backups and certification only on request; this requires deletion in 30 days with written confirmation without request and no backup extension.

commitments.quote: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance with this VDPA once per calendar year on thirty (30) days' notice, and within ten (10) days after notice following a Data Incident.
commitments.summary: Retailer may audit Vendor's compliance once per calendar year on 30 days' notice and within 10 days after notice following a Data Incident.

deadline.anchor: annual audit (Retailer's notice period)

secondary_deadline.anchor: Retailer's notice following a Data Incident

commitments.scope: Vendor's compliance with the VDPA; routine annual audit and post-Data Incident audit.
commitments.deviation: Baseline limits audits to reports plus one on-site audit per 12 months only if a supervisory authority requires, on 60 days' notice at Customer's expense; this gives an annual audit right without regulator trigger, 30 days' notice, and a 10-day post-incident audit. Cost allocation is not stated. Baseline 9.2 annual penetration test has no equivalent.

commitments.quote: This VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.summary: The VDPA binds and benefits each party's successors and permitted assigns.
commitments.scope: Successors and permitted assigns of both parties.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: A change of control of Vendor, by merger, acquisition or otherwise, does not terminate or modify this VDPA. Any acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data unless Retailer agrees in writing.
commitments.summary: A change of control of Vendor does not end or modify the VDPA, and an acquirer's standard terms do not apply to Retailer Data without Retailer's written agreement.
commitments.scope: Change of control of Vendor by merger, acquisition or otherwise; acquirer's standard terms.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent for change-of-control protection; related to order of precedence.

commitments.quote:
| Amazon Web Services, Inc. | Hosting | United States |
| Helpdesk Platform, Inc. | Support ticketing | United States |
commitments.summary: Approved Subprocessors are AWS (hosting) and Helpdesk Platform, Inc. (support ticketing), both in the United States.
commitments.scope: Approved Subprocessors permitted to process Retailer Data without further consent.
commitments.deviation: Baseline publishes a Subprocessor list on the Trust Center with general authorization; this is a fixed contractual list requiring consent for additions.

commitments.quote: | ExampleCo, Inc. (Vendor Affiliate) | Platform hosting and AI features for the Services | United States |
commitments.summary: Amendment No. 1 (September 8, 2025) added ExampleCo, Inc., a Vendor Affiliate, as an approved Subprocessor for platform hosting and AI features, located in the United States.
commitments.scope: ExampleCo is a Subprocessor under 2.4 so the Subprocessor duties, 24-hour incident notice, and AI training restriction in 3.2 apply to it. Its approval is limited to platform hosting and AI features.
commitments.deviation: Baseline gives general authorization and a Trust Center list; this adds a specific Affiliate by written amendment, with purpose and location limits. Baseline AI terms 8.1 and 8.3 are displaced by 3.2 for Retailer Data.

commitments.quote: This Addendum controls over any conflicting term of the Agreement, any order form, and any data processing addendum, privacy policy, or other document published or provided by Supplier. Terms incorporated by reference to a Supplier website, including any Supplier trust or security site, do not bind Bank and do not modify this Addendum.
commitments.summary: The Addendum overrides the Agreement, order forms, any Supplier DPA and Supplier website or trust-site terms, which cannot modify it.
commitments.scope: All conflicting terms in the Agreement, order forms and Supplier-provided documents, including the Supplier DPA and trust-site terms. Type chosen by inference, since the clause affects incident, subprocessor and other duties.
commitments.deviation: The DPA says it controls over the Agreement for personal data processing; here the Addendum controls over the DPA and trust-site terms are expressly not binding.

commitments.quote: "Bank Data" means all data and information, in any form, that Supplier or any Subcontractor receives, accesses, creates or processes in connection with the Agreement, including (a) data provided by or on behalf of Bank or its customers; (b) metadata, logs and configuration data relating to Bank's use of the Services; and (c) any data derived from any of the foregoing, including model outputs, embeddings, annotations, and data that has been aggregated, de-identified, pseudonymized or tokenized.
commitments.summary: Protected Bank Data covers all data processed under the Agreement, including metadata, logs, derived data, model outputs and aggregated or de-identified data.
commitments.scope: Defines what data the duties apply to; aggregated or de-identified data stays covered. Type chosen by inference because it chiefly affects AI-use limits.
commitments.deviation: The DPA covers only Personal Data in Customer Data and treats aggregated or de-identified Usage Data as outside its scope (1.6, 8.2); here derived, de-identified and aggregated data and metadata are covered.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a written information security program that is consistent with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and the FFIEC Information Technology Examination Handbook.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a written security program consistent with NIST CSF and the FFIEC IT Handbook.
commitments.deviation: The DPA commits to the Annex 2 measures, which Supplier may update; here a written program aligned to named frameworks is required.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall encrypt Bank Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Supplier must encrypt Bank Data at rest with AES-256 or stronger and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data (broad definition).
commitments.deviation: Substantively the same standard as Annex 2, but applied to the broader Bank Data and phrased as 'AES-256 or stronger'.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access to systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require MFA for all remote access to systems handling Bank Data.
commitments.scope: Systems that store, process or transmit Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires MFA for production system access; here MFA is required for all remote access to any system handling Bank Data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall complete a criminal background check on all Supplier Personnel before granting them access to Bank Data, to the extent permitted by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier must run criminal background checks on all personnel, including Subcontractor personnel, before granting access to Bank Data, where law permits.

deadline.anchor: granting Supplier Personnel access to Bank Data

commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel includes employees, contractors and agents of Supplier and of any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain throughout the term of the Agreement a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services.
commitments.summary: Supplier must keep a current SOC 2 Type II report for the Services throughout the term.
commitments.scope: The Services.
commitments.deviation: The DPA also commits to ISO/IEC 27001 certification; this contract requires only SOC 2 Type II.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall store and process Bank Data only within the United States.
commitments.summary: Bank Data must be stored and processed only in the United States.
commitments.scope: All Bank Data, including data held by Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA stores data in the customer-selected region and allows access from elsewhere; here storage and processing are restricted to the US.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any Supplier Personnel located outside the United States to access Bank Data, including for support or maintenance, without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.summary: No personnel outside the US, including Subcontractor personnel, may access Bank Data without Bank's prior written approval.
commitments.scope: Supplier Personnel includes Subcontractor personnel; covers support and maintenance access.
commitments.deviation: The DPA permits offshore access for support, maintenance and security, including from Manila; here it is prohibited absent prior written approval.

commitments.quote: Supplier may permit only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 ("Approved Subcontractors") to access Bank Data, and each only within the scope stated for it in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: Only the Subcontractors listed in Schedule 2 may access Bank Data, each only within its listed scope.
commitments.scope: Subcontractor includes any Supplier Affiliate and any third party with access to Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives general authorization to engage Subprocessors; here only a closed, scope-limited list is allowed.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give Bank's Third-Party Risk Management office at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice, delivered as provided in Exhibit C, before adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope.
commitments.summary: Supplier must give Bank's TPRM office 90 days' prior written notice before adding or replacing a Subcontractor or expanding an approved scope.

deadline.anchor: adding or replacing any Subcontractor or expanding an Approved Subcontractor's scope

commitments.recipient: Bank Third-Party Risk Management office, email tprm-notices@anb.example, with a copy to Awesome National Bank, N.A., Legal Department, 100 Example Plaza, New York, NY 10001
commitments.scope: Additions, replacements and scope expansions; no urgent-replacement exception is stated.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 30 days' notice via Trust Center update and email to subscribers; here 90 days' direct written notice to a named office, and no Trust Center notice or urgent-replacement carve-out (5.4).

commitments.quote: Bank may object within thirty (30) days after receiving the notice. If Bank objects, Supplier shall not engage the Subcontractor for the Services provided to Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
commitments.summary: Bank may object within 30 days of notice; if it does, Supplier must not engage the Subcontractor for Bank, or Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty and with a pro-rata refund.

deadline.anchor: Bank's receipt of the Subcontractor notice

commitments.scope: Affected Services.
commitments.deviation: The DPA objection window is 15 days, requires reasonable data protection grounds, and termination is the sole remedy; here 30 days, no stated grounds, the Subcontractor is not engaged on objection, and termination carries a pro-rata refund.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall impose on each Subcontractor written obligations at least as protective of Bank Data as this Addendum.
commitments.summary: Supplier must flow down written obligations at least as protective as the Addendum to each Subcontractor.
commitments.scope: Each Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: The DPA only states Supplier remains responsible for Subprocessors; it has no explicit flow-down standard.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within six (6) hours after the Subcontractor's Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must require each Subcontractor to notify Supplier of any Security Incident within 6 hours of the Subcontractor's Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Subcontractor's Discovery (earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident)

commitments.scope: Any Security Incident (actual or reasonably suspected) known to a Subcontractor. This period binds Subcontractors, not Supplier's notice to Bank.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier remains fully liable to Bank for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Supplier is fully liable to Bank for its Subcontractors' acts and omissions.
commitments.scope: All Subcontractors.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes Supplier responsible for Subprocessors' performance of DPA obligations; here liability is full and covers all acts and omissions.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and in no event later than twelve (12) hours after Discovery.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify Bank of any Security Incident as soon as possible and within 12 hours of Discovery.

deadline.anchor: Discovery: the earliest time Supplier or any Subcontractor knew, or by reasonable diligence would have known, of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center: telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147; email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example
commitments.scope: Any actual or reasonably suspected Security Incident involving Bank Data or any Supplier or Subcontractor system that stores, processes or transmits it, whether or not access to Bank Data is confirmed. Under 6.8 this shortest period controls over longer ones such as the 72 hours in D.2.
commitments.deviation: The DPA gives 72 hours after Supplier confirms a Personal Data Breach; here 12 hours after Discovery, which includes constructive knowledge and Subcontractor knowledge, and covers suspected incidents.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall give notice under Section 6.1 by telephone and by email to Bank's Cyber Fusion Center as provided in Exhibit C. Notice provided only to Bank's relationship manager, or through a Supplier status page or trust site, does not satisfy Section 6.1.
commitments.summary: Incident notice must be given by both telephone and email to the Cyber Fusion Center; notice only to the relationship manager or via status or trust pages does not count.
commitments.recipient: Bank Cyber Fusion Center: telephone (24x7) +1 (212) 555-0147; email cfc-thirdparty@anb.example (relationship manager Dana Okafor is for routine matters only)
commitments.scope: Notices under Section 6.1.
commitments.deviation: The DPA sends notice to the customer-designated security contact or account owner; here phone plus email to the Cyber Fusion Center is mandated.

commitments.quote: Supplier's initial notice shall include all information then known about the Security Incident, including the date and time of Discovery, the systems and Subcontractors involved, and the categories of Bank Data affected or potentially affected.
commitments.summary: The initial notice must include all known information, including Discovery time, systems and Subcontractors involved, and Bank Data categories affected or potentially affected.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents as defined.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires nature, categories of data and measures to the extent known; here all known information plus Discovery time and systems and Subcontractors involved.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall provide written status updates at least once every twenty-four (24) hours until the Security Incident is contained
commitments.summary: Supplier must give written status updates at least every 24 hours until the incident is contained.

deadline.anchor: initial notice, until the Security Incident is contained

commitments.scope: Each Security Incident until containment.
commitments.deviation: The DPA only says further information will be provided as available; here written updates are required every 24 hours.

commitments.quote: shall deliver a written root-cause report within thirty (30) days after containment.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver a written root-cause report within 30 days after containment.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.scope: Each Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not notify any Bank customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media of a Security Incident involving Bank Data without Bank's prior written consent, unless required by law.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not notify Bank customers, regulators, law enforcement or the media of an incident without Bank's prior written consent unless law requires.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents involving Bank Data; exception where required by law.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where law requires such notice, Supplier shall inform Bank before giving it, to the extent legally permitted.
commitments.summary: Where law requires Supplier to notify third parties, Supplier must first inform Bank, to the extent legally permitted.

deadline.anchor: Supplier giving legally required notice to a customer, regulator, law enforcement agency or the media

commitments.scope: Legally required third-party notices only.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall preserve all logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident for at least one (1) year after containment, and shall give Bank and its designated forensic investigator access to that evidence on request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must preserve forensic evidence for at least one year after containment and give Bank and its forensic investigator access on request.

deadline.anchor: containment of the Security Incident

commitments.recipient: Bank and its designated forensic investigator
commitments.scope: Logs, images and other forensic evidence relating to a Security Incident.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall reimburse Bank's reasonable costs of investigating and responding to a Security Incident caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor, including costs of notifying affected individuals and providing them with twenty-four (24) months of credit monitoring.
commitments.summary: Supplier must reimburse Bank's reasonable investigation and response costs for incidents it or a Subcontractor causes, including notification and 24 months of credit monitoring.
commitments.scope: Security Incidents caused by Supplier or any Subcontractor.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent; the DPA 7.4 only says notification is not an admission of fault.

commitments.quote: Supplier's obligations to ANB Securities LLC are supplemented by Exhibit D.
commitments.summary: Supplier's obligations to ANB Securities LLC are supplemented by Exhibit D.
commitments.scope: ANB Securities LLC (an Affiliate of Bank).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Where this Addendum, the Agreement, any exhibit or schedule, or applicable law specifies more than one period for the same notice, the shortest period applies.
commitments.summary: When several periods apply to the same notice, the shortest controls.
commitments.scope: Applies across the Addendum, Agreement, exhibits, schedules and law; makes the 12-hour period in 6.1 control over D.2's 72 hours (inference as to application to ANB Securities, an Affiliate of Bank).
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall notify ANB Securities LLC as soon as possible, but no later than seventy-two (72) hours after becoming aware of a breach in security resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system maintained by Supplier.
commitments.summary: Supplier must notify ANB Securities LLC within 72 hours after becoming aware of a breach resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system it maintains.

deadline.anchor: Supplier becoming aware of a breach in security resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system maintained by Supplier

commitments.recipient: ANB Securities LLC (no contact details given in the contract)
commitments.scope: Supplier's processing of customer information of ANB Securities LLC, a registered broker-dealer (D.1). Displaced by the shorter 12-hour period under 6.8 and D.3 (inference that such breaches also fall within Security Incident).
commitments.deviation: Same 72-hour length as the DPA, but runs from Supplier's awareness of the breach rather than confirmation, and is not the governing period because 6.8 applies the shortest period.

commitments.quote: This Exhibit supplements, and does not replace, Section 6 of the Addendum.
commitments.summary: Exhibit D adds to Section 6 and does not replace it.
commitments.scope: ANB Securities LLC customer information.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any artificial intelligence or machine learning model, other than a model used solely to provide the Services to Bank.
commitments.summary: Supplier may not use Bank Data to train, fine-tune, evaluate or improve any AI/ML model except one used solely to serve Bank.
commitments.scope: Bank Data as defined, including derived, aggregated and de-identified data; any AI/ML model.
commitments.deviation: The DPA bars only training or fine-tuning of foundation models made available to other customers and permits use of Usage Data; here all AI/ML training, evaluation and improvement is barred, including with aggregated or de-identified data.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall not permit any person to review, label or annotate Bank Data for the purpose of developing or improving any model, except as expressly permitted for an Approved Subcontractor in Schedule 2.
commitments.summary: No one may review, label or annotate Bank Data to develop or improve models, except as Schedule 2 expressly permits for an Approved Subcontractor.
commitments.scope: Bank Data; the Schedule 2 exception applies to Labelforge's de-identified feedback samples.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall identify in Schedule 2 every third-party model provider that receives Bank Data, and shall ensure that no model provider retains Bank Data after returning a response.
commitments.summary: Supplier must list every third-party model provider receiving Bank Data in Schedule 2 and ensure none retains Bank Data after responding.
commitments.scope: Third-party model providers receiving Bank Data.
commitments.deviation: The DPA lists providers on the Trust Center and allows retention for abuse monitoring; here the list is in Schedule 2 and no retention is allowed after the response.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least once every twelve (12) months, and shall deliver an executive summary of the results to Bank within thirty (30) days after Bank's request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must have an independent penetration test done at least every 12 months and deliver an executive summary to Bank within 30 days of request.

deadline.anchor: previous penetration test

secondary_deadline.anchor: Bank's request for the executive summary

commitments.scope: The Services.
commitments.deviation: Same annual cadence, but the summary is delivered to Bank on request within 30 days rather than made available on the Trust Center.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall remediate vulnerabilities rated Critical within fifteen (15) days, and vulnerabilities rated High within thirty (30) days, after identification.
commitments.summary: Supplier must remediate Critical vulnerabilities within 15 days and High vulnerabilities within 30 days of identification.

deadline.anchor: identification of a Critical vulnerability

commitments.scope: Vulnerabilities rated Critical or High.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall deliver its SOC 2 Type II report to Bank within thirty (30) days after the report is issued, and a bridge letter on request.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver each SOC 2 Type II report to Bank within 30 days of issuance and a bridge letter on request.

deadline.anchor: issuance of the SOC 2 Type II report

commitments.scope: SOC 2 Type II report and bridge letter.
commitments.deviation: The DPA makes the report available via the Trust Center under NDA terms; here it is proactively delivered to Bank within 30 days, plus bridge letters.

commitments.quote: Bank, its auditors and its regulators may audit Supplier's compliance with this Addendum once in any twelve (12) month period on thirty (30) days' written notice, and at any time after a Security Incident on five (5) business days' written notice. Nothing in this Addendum limits the access of any regulator with authority over Bank.
commitments.summary: Bank, its auditors and regulators may audit once per 12 months on 30 days' notice and at any time after a Security Incident on 5 business days' notice, and regulator access is not limited.

deadline.anchor: routine audit (written notice by Bank)

secondary_deadline.anchor: post-Security Incident audit (written notice by Bank)

commitments.scope: Compliance with the Addendum; Bank, its auditors and its regulators.
commitments.deviation: The DPA treats reports as satisfying audit rights, with an on-site audit only where a supervisory authority requires it, on 60 days' notice; here a direct annual audit right on 30 days' notice, a post-incident audit on 5 business days' notice, and unrestricted regulator access.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan for the Services with a recovery time objective of no more than four (4) hours and a recovery point objective of no more than one (1) hour.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain a BC/DR plan with a recovery time objective of at most 4 hours and recovery point objective of at most 1 hour.
commitments.scope: The Services.
commitments.deviation: The DPA requires a BC/DR plan without specified RTO or RPO; here RTO is 4 hours and RPO 1 hour.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall test the plan at least annually, provide Bank a summary of the results, and participate in Bank's annual operational resilience exercise on sixty (60) days' written notice.
commitments.summary: Supplier must test the plan at least annually, give Bank a summary of results, and take part in Bank's annual resilience exercise on 60 days' notice.

deadline.anchor: previous plan test

secondary_deadline.anchor: Bank's annual operational resilience exercise (written notice by Bank)

commitments.scope: BC/DR plan for the Services.
commitments.deviation: Same annual testing, but adds sharing results with Bank and participating in Bank's resilience exercise.

commitments.quote: Supplier shall maintain cyber liability insurance with limits of no less than twenty-five million dollars ($25,000,000) per claim throughout the term of the Agreement and for two (2) years after.
commitments.summary: Supplier must maintain cyber liability insurance of at least $25,000,000 per claim during the term and for two years after.

deadline.anchor: end of the term of the Agreement

commitments.scope: Cyber liability insurance, $25,000,000 per claim minimum.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Within thirty (30) days after termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request, Supplier shall return Bank Data to Bank in the format Bank reasonably requests and then securely destroy all Bank Data, including in backups, held by Supplier and its Subcontractors.
commitments.summary: Within 30 days after termination or Bank's written request, Supplier must return Bank Data and then securely destroy all of it, including backups and Subcontractor copies.

deadline.anchor: termination of the Agreement or Bank's written request

commitments.scope: All Bank Data held by Supplier and Subcontractors, including backups.
commitments.deviation: The DPA deletes within 90 days after termination, with backups overwritten within a further 35 days and no return; here 30 days, return first, backups included, and triggered also by Bank's request.

commitments.quote: Within ten (10) business days after destruction, Supplier shall deliver a certificate of destruction signed by an officer of Supplier.
commitments.summary: Supplier must deliver an officer-signed certificate of destruction within 10 business days after destruction.

deadline.anchor: destruction of Bank Data

commitments.deviation: The DPA provides certification only on request; here it is automatic within 10 business days and must be officer-signed.

commitments.quote: Sections 6, 10 and 11 survive termination of the Agreement for as long as Supplier or any Subcontractor holds Bank Data.
commitments.summary: The incident, insurance and return/destruction sections survive termination while Supplier or any Subcontractor holds Bank Data.
commitments.scope: Sections 6, 10 and 11. Type chosen by inference as the clause spans incident, insurance and deletion duties.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: All Bank Data, US regions only
commitments.summary: Amazon Web Services, Inc. (infrastructure hosting, United States) may access all Bank Data, in US regions only.
commitments.scope: Amazon Web Services, Inc.; infrastructure hosting; location United States.
commitments.deviation: The DPA relies on a published Trust Center list with general authorization; here scope and location are fixed in the schedule.

commitments.quote: Prompts and outputs only; zero retention
commitments.summary: Model Provider A, Inc. (large-model inference for AI agent features) may handle only prompts and outputs, with zero retention.
commitments.scope: Model Provider A, Inc.; location United States.
commitments.deviation: The DPA allows model provider retention for abuse monitoring; here zero retention.

commitments.quote: Only de-identified feedback samples that Bank submits through the Services' feedback feature, for improving Bank's own agents. Bank Data in identifiable form is not permitted.
commitments.summary: Labelforge, Inc. may annotate only de-identified feedback samples Bank submits via the feedback feature, to improve Bank's own agents; identifiable Bank Data is not permitted.
commitments.scope: Labelforge, Inc.; human annotation; United States, US-based annotators only. This is the Schedule 2 exception to Section 7.2.
commitments.deviation: No DPA equivalent.

commitments.quote: Contact details of Bank users only
commitments.summary: Helpdesk Platform, Inc. (support ticketing) may access only contact details of Bank users.
commitments.scope: Helpdesk Platform, Inc.; location United States.
commitments.deviation: The DPA has no per-subprocessor data scope limits.

commitments.quote: This DPA applies only to ExampleCo's processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.summary: The DPA's duties cover only Customer Personal Data that ExampleCo processes, not other Customer Data.
commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data only, meaning Personal Data contained in Customer Data that ExampleCo processes on Customer's behalf in providing the Services.

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will process Customer Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions, which are set out in the Agreement, this DPA, and Customer's configuration of the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must process Customer Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions.
commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will ensure that personnel authorized to process Customer Personal Data are bound by written obligations of confidentiality.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must bind personnel who process Customer Personal Data to written confidentiality obligations.
commitments.scope: Personnel authorized to process Customer Personal Data

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will implement and maintain the technical and organizational measures described in Annex 2 ("Security Measures"). ExampleCo may update the Security Measures from time to time, provided that updates do not materially reduce the overall security of the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain the Annex 2 security measures and may update them only if overall security is not materially reduced.
commitments.scope: The Services; measures described in Annex 2

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Services, or successor standards that are substantially equivalent.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO/IEC 27001 certification, or substantially equivalent successors.
commitments.scope: The Services

commitments.quote: Customer grants ExampleCo general authorization to engage Subprocessors. The current list of Subprocessors is published on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: Customer gives general authorization for ExampleCo to engage Subprocessors, and the current list is published on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Subprocessors, meaning any third party engaged by ExampleCo that processes Customer Personal Data

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will give notice of any new Subprocessor at least thirty (30) days before the new Subprocessor begins processing Customer Personal Data, by updating the Trust Center list and emailing Customers who have subscribed to Subprocessor updates on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must give at least 30 days' notice of a new Subprocessor by updating the Trust Center list and emailing subscribed Customers.

deadline.anchor: the new Subprocessor begins processing Customer Personal Data

commitments.recipient: Customers who have subscribed to Subprocessor updates on the Trust Center (also published on the Trust Center list at trust.exampleco.example)
commitments.scope: New Subprocessors that will process Customer Personal Data

commitments.quote: Customer may object to a new Subprocessor on reasonable data protection grounds by written notice within fifteen (15) days after ExampleCo's notice. If the parties cannot resolve the objection within thirty (30) days, Customer may terminate the affected Services as its sole and exclusive remedy.
commitments.summary: Customer may object in writing within 15 days of notice, and if unresolved after 30 days may terminate the affected Services as its sole remedy.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo's notice of the new Subprocessor

secondary_deadline.anchor: the objection (inference: the clause does not state the start of the 30 days)

commitments.scope: Objections on reasonable data protection grounds to a new Subprocessor; termination of the affected Services only

commitments.quote: Where ExampleCo must replace a Subprocessor urgently to protect the security or continuity of the Services, ExampleCo may do so without prior notice and will notify Customer promptly afterward.
commitments.summary: For urgent security or continuity replacements, ExampleCo may skip prior notice but must notify Customer promptly afterward.

deadline.anchor: the urgent replacement of the Subprocessor

commitments.scope: Urgent Subprocessor replacements to protect security or continuity of the Services

commitments.quote: ExampleCo remains responsible for its Subprocessors' performance of the obligations in this DPA.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo stays responsible for its Subprocessors' performance of the DPA obligations.
commitments.scope: All Subprocessors

commitments.quote: Customer Personal Data will be stored at rest in the hosting region Customer selects for its Services.
commitments.summary: Customer Personal Data is stored at rest in the hosting region Customer selects.
commitments.scope: Storage at rest of Customer Personal Data; does not restrict access from elsewhere (see 6.2)

commitments.quote: ExampleCo personnel and Subprocessors may access Customer Personal Data from locations outside the selected hosting region to provide support, maintenance and security operations, including from ExampleCo's support center in Manila, Philippines. Any transfer is made under the transfer mechanism in Annex 3.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo personnel and Subprocessors may access Customer Personal Data from outside the hosting region, including Manila, for support, maintenance and security, with transfers under the Annex 3 mechanism.
commitments.scope: Remote access for support, maintenance and security operations, including from Manila, Philippines

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must notify Customer without undue delay and within 72 hours after ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach.

deadline.anchor: ExampleCo confirms a Personal Data Breach (ExampleCo's own confirmation starts the clock)

commitments.scope: Personal Data Breach: a breach of security of the Services that ExampleCo has confirmed led to accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorized disclosure of, or access to, Customer Personal Data; excludes unsuccessful attempts and activities that do not compromise security, such as unsuccessful log-ins, pings, port scans and denial-of-service attacks

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will send notice to the security contact Customer designates in the Services administration console. If no security contact is designated, ExampleCo will send notice to Customer's account owner.
commitments.summary: Breach notice goes to Customer's designated security contact, or to the account owner if none is designated.
commitments.recipient: The security contact Customer designates in the Services administration console; otherwise Customer's account owner (no contact details given)
commitments.scope: Personal Data Breach notices

commitments.quote: ExampleCo's notice will describe, to the extent then known, the nature of the Personal Data Breach, the categories of data affected, and the measures taken or proposed to address it. ExampleCo will provide further information as it becomes available.
commitments.summary: The breach notice must describe the nature, data categories affected and measures, and ExampleCo must provide further information as it becomes available.
commitments.scope: Personal Data Breach notice content and follow-up information

commitments.quote: ExampleCo's notification of or response to a Personal Data Breach is not an acknowledgment of fault or liability.
commitments.summary: Notifying or responding to a Personal Data Breach is not an admission of fault or liability.
commitments.scope: Personal Data Breach notification and response

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune any foundation model that is made available to other customers.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must not use Customer Data to train or fine-tune foundation models made available to other customers.
commitments.scope: Customer Data (not limited to Customer Personal Data); foundation models made available to other customers

commitments.quote: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo may use Usage Data to operate, secure and improve the Services.
commitments.scope: Usage Data: aggregated or de-identified data about use and performance of the Services that does not identify Customer or any natural person

commitments.quote: ExampleCo lists the third-party model providers used by AI features as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: Third-party AI model providers are listed as Subprocessors on the Trust Center.
commitments.scope: Third-party model providers used by AI features

commitments.quote: ExampleCo requires its model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond the time needed to return a response, except as required for abuse monitoring.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must require model providers not to retain prompts or outputs beyond returning a response, except for abuse monitoring.
commitments.scope: Prompts and outputs handled by third-party model providers; abuse monitoring exception

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will make its most recent SOC 2 Type II report available to Customer through the Trust Center, subject to Customer's acceptance of the Trust Center non-disclosure terms.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must make its latest SOC 2 Type II report available via the Trust Center, subject to the Trust Center NDA terms.
commitments.scope: Most recent SOC 2 Type II report

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will engage an independent third party to perform a penetration test of the Services at least annually and will make an executive summary of the results available through the Trust Center.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must have an independent third party penetration test the Services at least annually and publish an executive summary on the Trust Center.

deadline.anchor: each penetration test (at least annually)

commitments.scope: Penetration test of the Services; executive summary of results

commitments.quote: Customer agrees that the reports in Sections 9.1 and 9.2 satisfy any audit right under Data Protection Laws.
commitments.summary: Customer agrees that the SOC 2 report and penetration test summary satisfy any audit right under Data Protection Laws.
commitments.scope: Audit rights under Data Protection Laws

commitments.quote: Where a supervisory authority requires a further audit, Customer may conduct one on-site audit per twelve (12) month period, with at least sixty (60) days' written notice, during business hours, and at Customer's expense.
commitments.summary: If a supervisory authority requires a further audit, Customer may conduct one on-site audit per 12 months on at least 60 days' written notice, during business hours, at its own expense.

deadline.anchor: the on-site audit

secondary_deadline.anchor: each twelve month period (one audit allowed)

commitments.scope: On-site audit only where a supervisory authority requires a further audit

commitments.quote: Within ninety (90) days after termination or expiry of the Agreement, ExampleCo will delete Customer Personal Data from the Services. Backups are overwritten in the ordinary course within a further thirty-five (35) days.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must delete Customer Personal Data within 90 days after termination or expiry, with backups overwritten within a further 35 days.

deadline.anchor: termination or expiry of the Agreement

secondary_deadline.anchor: the end of the 90-day deletion period (backup overwrite)

commitments.scope: Customer Personal Data in the Services and in backups

commitments.quote: ExampleCo will provide written certification of deletion upon Customer's written request.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must provide written certification of deletion when Customer requests it in writing.
commitments.scope: Deletion of Customer Personal Data

commitments.quote: If this DPA conflicts with the Agreement, this DPA controls as to the processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.summary: The DPA prevails over the Agreement on conflicts concerning processing of Customer Personal Data.
commitments.scope: Processing of Customer Personal Data

commitments.quote: Customer Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.summary: Customer Data must be encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher.
commitments.scope: Customer Data

commitments.quote: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.summary: Access to production systems requires multi-factor authentication.
commitments.scope: Production systems

commitments.quote: ExampleCo maintains a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and tests it at least annually.
commitments.summary: ExampleCo must maintain a business continuity and disaster recovery plan and test it at least annually.

deadline.anchor: each test of the plan (at least annually)

commitments.scope: Business continuity and disaster recovery plan
